texts: mixed: the main claim lands well - the being-visible state is reified with the six-cat group, the cliff-spires, the morning, day 155 and Year 1 all attached, and past tense on it - but the rule that hands visibility down to each of the six cats concludes a tenseless atom, so every cat reads as visible now rather than on that morning. That is our slip on a shape the instruction set licenses, not anything your wording forced, so no rewrite is called for. One thing worth knowing: 'day 155 of Year 1' currently reuses the day-of-month term, so no content is lost but the engine cannot yet order your dates by day-of-year.

bad: three separate losses ride on this one sentence. 'About twenty' has no licensed approximate-count form, so the hedge lands in a slot that takes a plain integer; the count then sits on one shared feather group under a daily recurrence, which says the very same twenty feathers were collected every morning; and 'in that week' is dropped altogether, so a one-week habit is recorded as a standing daily one. Splitting the habit from the count and naming the window in days fixes all three: 'Tessa Brae collected feathers every morning from day 152 to day 158 of Year 1. On the morning of day 155 of Year 1 she collected twenty feathers.' Use whichever day numbers that week actually spans, and an exact figure - a hedged count ('about twenty') and a per-occasion count ('twenty per morning') each have no carrier at all, so either one is simply dropped.

good. the reporting is a past event with Tessa Brae as its holder and the Council as recipient, and the whole 'had begun to return' complement is sealed under it - the past perfect kept inside the seal, the per-cat distribution carried as a sealed conjunct - so nothing about the sky-cats' return is asserted as fact, only as what she reported.

mixed: the ask-to-consider structure is handled exactly as intended - the considering is reified in its own right, tenseless, with the Council copied in as the one who would consider and Halden as what is considered - but 'a permanent station' mints a top-level witness, so the parse asserts that a permanent station exists when your sentence only proposes one. Dropping the article keeps the proposal non-committal: 'Bevin Coombe asked the Council to consider Halden for permanent station duty.'

bad: 'since the wraith' anchors the interval on a creature rather than on a time or an event, so the parse drops the wraith witness into the interval's start slot and 'when did the tending start?' would bind a wraith; under the rules the phrase has no carrier at all, which means it gets left out and the whole 'since' interval is lost. Name the event the phrase stands in for: 'Halden had tended the Stilllight Lantern well since the wraith appeared.' The rest of the sentence is right - the tending is past, ongoing, and well-done.

good. the approval is a past event with the Council as agent, the track as what was approved and Halden as the one it benefits; 'apprenticeship-completion track' is kept whole with its genus (a kind of track) exposed.
